subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosts
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: token volumes & target $/1M

Hi Alex — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on pricing benchmarks: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + routing; some search augmentation.
- Expected steady-state token volume: 5M–20M tokens/month (with spikes up to ~50M in Q4).
- Latency requirement: 200–500ms per response (p90).
- Data posture: logs retained 30 days, PII redaction required.

Pricing / budget context you shared:
- Target unit economics: ~$10/1M tokens (target)
- Procurement prefers committed/annual pricing if we can get to $8–$12/1M range for the committed tier.

What I’ll deliver by EOD tomorrow:
1) Preliminary $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and common open-model hosts.
2) A short cost breakdown showing where savings come from (batching, KV cache, quantized model variants, reserved capacity).
3) A proposed committed pricing tier and a one-page mutual action plan to route to procurement.

Attachments I’ll include: redwood_token_benchmark.xlsx (cost model), redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf (sample committed tiers).

If any of the volumes above are off, reply with the expected monthly token range and any hard budget constraints.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: token volumes & target $/1M

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Confirmed monthly target: we expect to start at ~7–10M tokens/month and ramp to 25–30M over 6 months if performance is solid.
- Budget: procurement wants to see committed pricing around $8–$10/1M tokens for planning; $10 is the internal target but we could accept $12 with clear ROI.
- Current benchmarking: we currently use a mix of Anthropic (sensitive flows) and a hosted open-model provider for bulk embedding/generation. Roughly what we pay today: Anthropic model averages ~$70–$90/1M tokens (sensitive flows), open-model host costs are closer to $25–$40/1M depending on quantization and commitment.

Please include a simple comparison row: Redwood expected committed price vs Anthropic vs OpenAI vs typical host-managed open model. Procurement will want the $/1M bucketed for 1M, 10M, 50M volumes.

Alex
VP Product, Acme Analytics
alex.j@acme-analytics.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing benchmark + unit-economics (attached)

Alex — attached the benchmark and the short cost model (redwood_token_benchmark.xlsx). Key highlights below: 

Benchmark (illustrative $/1M tokens) — committed tiers / typical public prices:
- Redwood (committed, 12mo, 20M/mo baseline): $9 / 1M tokens (baseline committed tier)
- Redwood (on-demand): $18 / 1M tokens (no commitment, additional overage tiers)
- Anthropic (sensitive flows, public list): ~$80 / 1M tokens (model-dependent)
- OpenAI (gpt-4-class or equivalent high-cap): ~$150 / 1M tokens for the most capable models; lighter models lower but still >$50/1M
- Host-managed open models (quantized, multi-tenant): $20–$35 / 1M tokens (depends on quantization, caching, and reserved capacity)

Unit-economics / where savings come from:
- Model selection & quantization: switching to an 8-bit quantized open model variant reduces raw compute cost by ~3–4x vs fp16 for many workloads.
- Batching & KV caching: expected effective token cost reduction 20–40% for conversational flows with prefix reuse.
- Reserved capacity: committed pools amortize GPU hours; at 20M tokens/month we can reach $9/1M or lower depending on model mix.

Attached: redwood_token_benchmark.xlsx (breakdown by model, GPU cost, cache impact) and redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf (sample committed tiers and SOW outline). Also adding a short mutual action plan (acme_mutual_action_plan.docx) that outlines procurement milestones + security questionnaire handoff.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a formal committed quote at $9/1M for a 12-month, 20M/mo baseline (DEAL-5821) — want to confirm that structure works for you.
2) If procurement wants lower $/1M, we can explore a stepped commitment (ramp discounts) or multi-year contract.
3) Procurement + legal review SOW and SOC2 evidence (I’ll loop our security team).

If that baseline sounds reasonable, I’ll circulate the quote and MAP to procurement today.

— Vanessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing benchmark + unit-economics (attached)

Vanessa / Aditya — quick internal note for the thread: proposing we offer Acme the following playbook to close quickly:

- Option A (12mo committed): 20M/mo baseline @ $9 / 1M tokens + 10% overage discount.
- Option B (24mo committed): 20M/mo baseline @ $8 / 1M tokens + 15% overage discount (needs exec approval).
- Include one month free onboarding credit and 90-day price protection for model variant swaps.

Rationale: volume profile and quick ramp justify a mid-commitment discount; keeps us competitive vs hosts while undercutting Anthropic/OpenAI by a wide margin for non-sensitive flows.

Marissa
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing benchmark + unit-economics (attached)

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement asked for: 
1) Formal quote + SOW reflecting Option A (20M baseline @ $9/1M) and Option B if exec approval is needed.
2) The benchmark sheet as a PDF for our finance team.
3) SOC2 and data-retention language for legal.

Please route the quote and SOW to procurement@acme-analytics.com and copy me. If you can get the SOC2 evidence link in the same email that would speed review.

We’re targeting a procurement review by 05/10; please confirm if your team can meet that timeline.

Best,
Alex
